Rokanuddin Mahmood with Murad Reza and Faisal M Faizee, Advocates— For the Petitioner 
TH Khan with Syed Ziaul Karim and Faisal H Khan, Advocates — For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Minhaz A Chowdhury ----- Informant-Petitioner
Vs.
Manzurul Huq & another ----- opposite Parties
full_judgment: 3. Upon the aforesaid allegations the petitioner lodged an FIR on 16.10.92 with the Ramna Police Station under sections 143/448/399/380/437/109 of the Penal Code against the said opposite party whereupon a GR case was started. The accused, thereafter, obtained bail on 4.11.92 from the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and he filed an application before the Magistrate under section 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for dispensing with his personal attendance before the court but the said application was rejected on the same date. The complainant petitioner then filed an application on 14.12.92 before the said Magistrate for cancellation of the bail. The accused opposite party remained absent on that date and consequently the learned Magistrate passed an order fixing 21.12.92 for hearing of the said application. The learned Magistrate directed the learned lawyer to produce the accused in court within 21.12.92 and he also directed the learned lawyer of the opposite party No. 1 for the surrender of his passport. The accused opposite party No.1 did not appear nor surrender his passport on 21.12.92. His learned lawyer filed another application under section 205 of the Code and also prayed for an adjournment of the hearing of the application for cancellation of the bail. The learned Magistrate rejected the said application under section 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on that date and the learned Magistrate again directed the learned lawyer to produce the accused and to surrender his passport on the next date fixing on 30.12.92. The accused opposite party No. 1 again filed an application on 29.12.92 under section 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the learned Magistrate was pleased to allow the said application dispensing with the personal attendance of the accused in court although he did not surrender the passport. On the next day i.e 30.12.92, the date fixed for hearing of the application for cancellation of the bail was heard and the learned Magistrate directed the learned lawyer for the accused opposite party to produce him in court on 16.1.93 for disposal of the said application; that on 16.1.93 the said opposite party did not appear before the court but got an application filed for time and the learned Magistrate again directed his lawyer to produce the accused in court on 24.1.93 and on that date the opposite party No. 1 was found absent and accordingly, the learned Magistrate cancelled his bail and issued warrant for his arrest. In the meantime the charge sheet was submitted in the said GR case on 13.2.93 and the same was accepted by the court. The learned Magistrate by his order dated 23.2.93 directed the surety of the accused opposite party to produce him in the court on 16.3.93 fixing for framing of the charge. The opposite party remained absent and consequently the trial was held in absentia and the judgment was passed on 21.7.93 convicting the accused opposite party and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for total period of 7 (seven) years. The accused thereafter surrendered before the Magistrate on 27.11.93 with a vokalatnama being attested by the court Sub-Inspector of Police with prayer for bail before the learned Magistrate to enable him to file an appeal against the said order of his conviction and sentence. The learned Magistrate rejected his prayer and ordered that he should be sent to jail and on that very day the accused opposite party moved the Sessions Judge for admitting the appeal upon condonation of delay and also prayed for bail. The learned Sessions Judge admitted the appeal on 27.11.93, condoned the delay and granted him bail which has been impugned in this revision.
